question: What is the main job of resuscitative equipment in the ward?

options.A: To provide routine daily patient hygiene care
options.B: To monitor long-term chronic wound healing
options.C: To manage sudden cardiac or respiratory arrest
options.D: To deliver oral medications during meals

explanation: You've got this! Resuscitative tools are kept ready specifically for emergencies when a patient stops breathing or their heart stops. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to know emergency devices very well before a crisis happens?

options.A: To prevent equipment theft in the ward
options.B: To ensure fast and effective action during high-stress moments
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To avoid having to document patient care tasks

explanation: Spot on! In an emergency, knowing your tools right away helps you act fast and save precious time. You are doing great! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a bag-valve-mask (BVM) resuscitator?

options.C: To visualize the vocal cords clearly

explanation: Great job! You squeeze the BVM manually to push air into the lungs of a patient who cannot breathe on their own. Simple and lifesaving! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h2)

question: A patient vomits heavily during a cardiac arrest. What should the nurse grab right away?
explanation: Well thought out! We must clear vomit immediately using suction so the airway is open and safe for breathing support. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which device delivers a shock to stop dangerous, irregular heart rhythms?
explanation: Exactly! The defibrillator sends a quick electrical current to reset a chaotic heart back into a steady rhythm. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why is setting up an IV line so crucial during a resuscitation?

options.A: To secure the endotracheal tube in place
options.B: To measure the exact volume of carbon dioxide exhaled
options.C: To monitor the patient's core body temperature
options.D: To deliver emergency medications and fluids directly into the bloodstream

explanation: Spot on! An IV line acts like a fast highway to pump life-saving drugs straight into circulation when every second counts. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h3)

question: How often should emergency crash carts and equipment usually be checked?

options.B: Only after a code blue occurs
options.C: At the start of every shift

explanation: Correct! Checking the crash cart every shift ensures everything is present, unexpired, and working before an emergency strikes. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h4)

question: What should you do immediately if you find an expired drug in the crash cart during a check?

options.A: Report and replace it right away
options.B: Leave it until the end of the week
options.C: Use it on the next stable patient
options.D: Hide it in the bottom drawer

explanation: You got it! Expired drugs can fail when you need them most, so swapping them out instantly keeps our patients safe. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is the best first step if an electrical piece of emergency gear fails to turn on?

options.A: Throw the device out the window
options.C: Check the power source and cable connections
options.D: Wait for a biomedical engineer to arrive

explanation: Brilliant! Often, it's just a loose plug or unseated battery that you can fix in seconds. Always check the basics first! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a good safety practice for emergency equipment?

options.D: Debriefing team performance after code events

explanation: Spot on! Never brush off small faults—minor issues can turn into big failures during a real emergency. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)
